channel.title: Hu Lab — English
channel.description: Hu Lab — Jerry Hu’s corner: casual notes, handy Python tools, and personally picked products and self-published books.

item.title: Brain Games That Do Not Feel Like Homework
item.description: Most puzzle books are either too easy for adults or too hard for casual play. Organ's Adventure finds a middle ground, with gentle challenges that build cognitive skills without the frustration.

item.title: Why Your Characterization Data Needs a Better Home Than Scattered Files
item.description: XRD patterns, SEM images, DSC curves, and TGA data are only useful if you can find them later. A structured characterization lab notebook bridges the gap between instrument output and meaningful analysis.

item.title: Keeping a Lab Notebook That Actually Helps in Semiconductor Processing
item.description: A review of why a structured lab notebook matters more in semiconductor processing than in most other engineering disciplines, and how the right notebook format saves time and prevents costly mistakes.

item.title: Why Thermodynamics Feels Harder Than It Is
item.description: Materials thermodynamics intimidates engineering students more than it should. The key is separating the conceptual core (free energy, equilibrium, phase stability) from the mathematical machinery used to calculate them.

item.title: Spectra Studio: A Free Spectral Plotting Tool for XRD, FTIR, RAMAN & DSC
item.description: A free spectral analysis and plotting tool for XRD, FTIR, RAMAN and DSC/TGA data — multi-format loading, peak fitting, phase matching and journal-ready figure export. This guide covers what it does, how to install it, and the difference between the Free and Pro editions.

item.title: How to Study Materials Science Without Drowning in Derivations
item.description: Materials science textbooks bury you in math before you grasp the concepts. Here is a different approach, using active recall and structured notes to learn crystal structures, phase diagrams, and mechanical properties.

item.title: The Tech Career Pivot That Actually Works
item.description: A review of the transition many tech workers face in their 30s and 40s. Not a crisis, but a real question about what comes next, and how to answer it without starting over.

item.title: Kyoto Without the Tourist Script
item.description: Most Kyoto guides send you to the same crowded spots. Here is a different approach to visiting Kyoto that focuses on timing, neighborhoods, and the experiences that reward the independent traveler.

item.title: Why Mediterranean Cooking Actually Works for Busy Families
item.description: The Mediterranean diet is consistently rated the worlds best diet. But can a family with picky eaters and tight schedules actually follow it? Yes, and here is how the planning works.

item.title: Five Bottlenecks Blocking 2D Semiconductors from the Fab
item.description: MoS₂, WS₂ and other 2D semiconductors promise to extend Moore's Law, but at least five industrialization bottlenecks stand between a lab-scale flake and a wafer-scale product.

item.title: Extra Income When Parenting Leaves No Free Time
item.description: Side hustles for parents face a constraint most guides ignore: you have limited time and it is not predictable. Here is a framework for income streams that work around parenting, not against it.

item.title: Why Your Solo Business Needs Different Money Rules
item.description: Personal finance advice for employees does not work for solopreneurs. Here is why the rules are different, and how to build a financial system that matches irregular income.

item.title: The Materials Science of Lithium-Ion Battery Recycling: Mining the Urban Mine
item.description: Battery recycling is not optional — 500,000 tons of Li-ion batteries will retire by 2025. But pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy, and direct regeneration each face different materials challenges.

item.title: The Materials Race in Carbon Capture: Amines, MOFs, and Zeolites
item.description: Carbon capture has been talked about for decades. The bottleneck is not engineering — it is materials chemistry.

item.title: The Real Bottleneck in Fusion Energy Isn't Plasma — It's Materials
item.description: Fusion reactors need materials that can withstand 150 million degrees and constant neutron bombardment. No known material can do this for long.

item.title: The Most Underestimated Bottleneck in Hydrogen Energy: Materials for Storage
item.description: Making hydrogen is solved. Storing and moving it is not — and materials science is the bottleneck nobody talks about.

item.title: The Materials Science of Data Storage: From HDDs to MRAM, PCM, and Beyond
item.description: Hard drives are approaching the superparamagnetic limit. MRAM, PCM, FeRAM, and RRAM each promise to replace them — but each is stuck on a different materials problem.

item.title: Perovskite Solar Cells: The Material Engineering Behind Record Efficiencies
item.description: Perovskite solar cells have leapt from 3.8% to over 26% efficiency in fifteen years — faster than silicon ever did. But stability and lead toxicity remain unsolved.

item.title: The Rare Earth Crisis vs Materials Substitution: Permanent Magnets for EV Motors
item.description: NdFeB is the strongest permanent magnet, but over 70% of rare earth supply comes from China. Alternative materials MnBi, MnAl, and ferrite each offer different tradeoffs.

item.title: The Materials Science of Solid-State Batteries: A Three-Way Tradeoff
item.description: Solid-state batteries promise safer, denser energy storage. But sulfide, oxide, and polymer electrolytes each face fundamental materials tradeoffs before mass production.

item.title: Thermoelectric Materials: Turning Waste Heat into Electricity — Why It Hasn't Taken Off
item.description: Thermoelectrics can convert waste heat directly into electricity. The problem is efficiency — and the materials tradeoffs that keep ZT values too low for commercial scale.

item.title: SiC and GaN: How Wide-Bandgap Semiconductors Are Reshaping EVs and Renewable Energy
item.description: SiC and GaN waited nearly a century for their moment. Now they power EV inverters and 5G base stations — but manufacturing defects still hold them back.

item.title: The Productivity Tools You Actually Keep Using
item.description: Most productivity tools promise to save time but end up adding cognitive overhead. Here is a framework for choosing tools that actually work, and why AI changes the calculation for knowledge workers.

item.title: SEM Particle Analyzer: Turning SEM Images into Real Size Distributions
item.description: A practical guide to the SEM Particle Analyzer: what problem it solves, who it is for, how to install and run it, and what you can do with the output.

item.title: Thesis Format Fixer: Get Your Word Thesis Format Right in One Pass
item.description: A practical guide to the Thesis Format Fixer: what pain it removes, who it is for, how to install and run it, and which formatting problems it fixes automatically.

item.title: Why Coloring Might Be the Most Underrated Way to Learn Sports Anatomy
item.description: How an illustrated coloring-and-labeling workbook turns passive reading into active recall for sports anatomy, athletic injuries, and rehabilitation. Built for physiotherapy students, athletic trainers, coaches, and athletes.
